subject: Ledgerly hosted evaluation — access checkpoints & limits
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@ledgerly.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Ledgerly hosted evaluation — access checkpoints & limits

Hi Samira,

Great to meet you and Tom on the call this morning — appreciate the clear runthrough of Ledgerly's first-use case (realtime invoice parsing + assisted categorization). As promised, quick recap of the open items we said we'd follow up on and recommended next steps for a Hosted API evaluation.

Summary of decisions from call:
- Preferred starting mode: Hosted API trial (you want to validate latency and cost quickly before considering Dedicated).
- Data residency: primary concern for EU customers — Ledgerly will route EU customer traffic to EU endpoints; we can provide a hosted EU region for the eval if needed.
- Rate envelope: expected peak of ~120 req/s during batch runs, but average 8–12 req/s.

Action items (recommended):
1) Quickstart sandbox access — we can provision a scoped hosted API key and two staging endpoints (us-west and eu-west) for a 14-day eval.
2) Endpoint mapping worksheet — Ben attached a short worksheet to capture your calling pattern (payload sizes, concurrency, KV cache expectations).
3) Ratecap proposal — baseline trial limits: 20 rps single-connection, token throttling at 60k tokens/min across trial; we can raise to 150 rps for constrained windows with a short escalation. Exact numbers final after you fill the worksheet.
4) Security/compliance — we'll send the SOC2 checklist and the network ops worksheet (attached). If you need Private deployment later, we'll route you to Dedicated/Private onboarding with a separate MSA.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- Today: Ben to share the network ops worksheet and quickstart checklist (attached).
- Wed: Ledgerly sends back the filled worksheet and any firewall CIDR/IP allowlist questions.
- Thu (if worksheet in): We provision sandbox keys and staging endpoints; client smoke test window scheduled for Fri.

Ben (cc'd) is on the technical thread for any infra or allowlist details. Samira/Tom — please reply with any immediate blockers or confirm you want the EU endpoint enabled for the trial.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments:
- redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
- network-ops-worksheet.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)
From: Samira Patel <samira@ledgerly.io>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@ledgerly.io>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Ledgerly hosted evaluation — access checkpoints & limits

Thanks Avery — and thanks Ben for jumping on. Quick answers from our side after internal sync: 

- Confirmed: we want to start with Hosted API to validate latency/cost.
- EU endpoint: yes please — Ledgerly processes EU customer invoices and we need to demonstrate residency for a pilot customer.
- Rate profile: the numbers you called out look reasonable. Two clarifications: (1) our peak 120 req/s estimate is for a nightly batch window that runs for ~18 minutes; (2) realtime interactive calls (web UI) are small payloads but bursty — expect bursts up to 60 rps for short periods.
- Security: we will need IP allowlist details and TLS cert chain info for our security review.

We’ll fill out the worksheet and return it by EOD Thu. If possible, can you include a short sample of the hosted endpoint URLs and the exact header key name for the sandbox API key (so our infra team can pre-configure)?

—Samira
Director of Product, Ledgerly
 samira@ledgerly.io
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@ledgerly.io>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@ledgerly.io>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ledgerly hosted evaluation — access checkpoints & limits

Hi Samira — quick technical follow-up, copying the exact bits you'll want for infra.

Sandboxing & endpoints:
- Staging endpoints (example):
  - us-west: https://staging-us.api.redwood.ai/v1/inference
  - eu-west: https://staging-eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/inference
- Header to set: Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY>
- Keys: we'll create one scoped API key for Ledgerly with read/write to the /v1/inference route and rate-limits applied. Key will be delivered via DocuSign-protected link (or secure HubSpot secret) if you prefer.

Rate limiting notes (trial defaults):
- Per-key baseline: 20 rps sustained, burst up to 60 rps per second for short windows (30s) without penalty.
- Batch window escalation: for your nightly 18-minute batch, we can temporarily raise sustained to 120 rps for that window once we confirm traffic pattern from worksheet.
- Token throttling: 60k tokens/min across the key during the trial; if you hit this we'll surface throttling events in the sandbox logs.

Network/allowlist items:
- IPs to allow (staging): 34.210.34.12, 35.177.21.9 (these are for the staging fleet; production IPs differ).
- TLS: standard public certs (Let's Encrypt in staging), production uses CA-signed certs.

Attachments: I attached the quickstart checklist and a one-page network ops worksheet for you to fill. If you'd rather have an S3-hosted tar with sample payloads we can add that too.

If you confirm you want the EU staging endpoint enabled now I’ll flip the switch and provision the API key. Otherwise I’ll wait for the filled worksheet.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments:
- redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf
- network-ops-worksheet.xlsx

Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 08:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Ledgerly hosted evaluation — access checkpoints & limits

Thanks — received everything. We reviewed the worksheet this morning and want the EU staging endpoint enabled from the start. Please provision the scoped sandbox key and send the allowlist IPs + exact DocuSign link for the key delivery.

We'll return the filled worksheet by EOD today. Also please enable the 120 rps nightly window option for the trial — we will only use it during the ~18-minute batch.

Tom
